- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility spike.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 85), model often overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged upward trend; cap forecast rise after peak or introduce early mean-reversion.
- If true outcome shows early mean-reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model continues upward; reduce forecast slope or introduce decay factor.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; add volatility buffer or use sentiment-weighted smoothing.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate sharp downward moves (especially after negative sentiment); add downward bias correction if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 1–2 days of +0.67 then -0.33), model overfits trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average or reduce forecast persistence.
